title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics with the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, provider-call accounting clarification, an artifact-grounded attribution of the single discordant episode, and narrowly scoped operational implications and reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to convert operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational adoption requires assurance that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic and semantic constraints, ordering/workflow invariants, and higher-order safety policies. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document these workflow-centred patterns and motivate the need for quantitative, artifact-grounded measures of the marginal value provided by runtime sandboxing [1]–[3].

Research question and contributions. We asked: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting; (3) a concise clarification of provider-call accounting semantics used for reproducible audit; (4) an artifact-grounded attribution of the single discordant episode; and (5) bounded operational recommendations describing when guarded stages are most likely to matter.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Recent survey and architectural reports argue that LLM generation must be combined with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts; they emphasize the multidimensional nature of correctness (syntax, command order, workflow invariants, and dynamic runtime properties) and call for workflow-centred evaluation [1].

Tool-focused case studies demonstrate that mature static analysers (configuration analyzers and NetKAT-like systems) progressively cover many static classes of errors but can still miss runtime-dependent behaviors; consequently, emulation or sandboxing is advocated as a complementary V&V primitive [2]. Prototype systems integrating generation with verification and execution harnesses report heterogeneous gains: some task regimes show most dangerous errors are caught by the verifier, while others reveal runtime failures only exposed by emulation [3]. These prior findings motivate our paired shared_initial_candidate design that isolates downstream guarded-stage effects from generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling (deterministic reseed up to two times for parser failures), multiplicity handling, contamination controls, and an analysis executor aligned with McNemar-style paired inference and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). The planned confirmatory size was Npairs = 720 and the minimum effect-of-interest for power planning was 0.20.

Tasks, model, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. Confirmatory tasks were deterministically generated from intent_configuration_repair_v1 covering three abstracted vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after allowed reseeds; no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory run. The requested/declared model was "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses); model_configuration archived requested max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature recorded as null (no explicit client temperature supplied). Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics we obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate per pair and presented that identical candidate to both downstream conditions, isolating downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations and the permitted repair-stage call) as the only sources of between-condition discordance.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implements deterministic rule-based intent-constraint checks: vendor-CLI syntactic parsing, canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break), protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance tests. The guarded pipeline runs that validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology, applies CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices, collects runtime observations (admin transitions, transient concurrent states, MTU/VLAN application effects, reachability consequences), and maps those observations to runtime-observation rules that can trigger additional guarded detections not encoded statically.

Provider-call audit: authoritative meaning and why counts appear as reported. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation include a provider-call audit that records model_calls_used = 721 and two related grouped counts: stage_counts and condition_counts. For clarity: (i) model_calls_used is the total number of hosted-model invocation events recorded during the run; (ii) stage_counts enumerates calls by orchestration stage (e.g., shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1); and (iii) condition_counts in the audit document summarizes provider-call attribution to logical stages (the archive records condition_counts:{"shared":720,"guarded":1}) rather than episode detection counts per experimental arm. In short, the audit fields reflect how many hosted-model calls occurred in each orchestration stage (shared initial + any repair calls) and do not replace the per-episode paired accounting presented in the analysis artifacts. Deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl together provide the authoritative per-episode linkage from pair_id → shared_initial candidate → any repair-stage provider call(s). The audit therefore supports the audited fact that there were 720 shared initial generations and a single repair-stage call (total model_calls_used = 721) during the confirmatory execution.

Analysis procedures. The primary analysis used the preregistered paired-binary executor: compute paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline), perform an exact McNemar two-sided test, and produce a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Complete_pair_primary handling (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs) was pre-registered; no irrecoverable pairs occurred, so primary results use all 720 pairs.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential outputs (artifact-grounded). The analysis artifacts report contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These values are verbatim from analysis/results.json and the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv).

Single discordant pair: artifact-grounded attribution. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. The unique discordant count n10 = 1 is therefore co-located with the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The canonical per-episode raw results (execution/raw_results.jsonl; input-results SHA-256 = df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) contain the specific pair_id and the repair_provider_trace field that link the guarded-only detection to that repair-stage event. The execution bundle thus permits an auditor to locate that unique pair and inspect whether the guarded detection arose from a guarded emulation observation or from the documented repair-stage transcript; the audit evidence records the repair-stage call as the only non-shared initial provider call in the confirmatory run.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show validator_trace objects with normalized_configuration, validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count = 0 for the majority of items. Those representative artifacts illustrate that the curated shared_initial candidates overwhelmingly complied with the validator’s rule set and that sandboxed emulation corroborated validator findings in this constrained task bank.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The archived artifacts support three artifact-grounded factors.

(1) Validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator explicitly encoded checks matching the curated task patterns (e.g., shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover). High baseline coverage (719/720) left virtually no headroom for the guarded stage to add detections in this constrained regime.

(2) Curated inclusion and low adversarial exposure. Confirmatory items were parser-validated and deterministically generated; there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions. This inclusion rule concentrates the sample where a strong validator is effective and underrepresents noisy or adversarial inputs where emulation often yields larger marginal gains.

(3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. By design the same sampled initial candidate was used in both conditions; provider-call auditing and deterministic_reconciliation show a single repair-stage call across all confirmatory pairs and that this single repair call corresponds to the sole guarded-only detection. Thus the observed n10 = 1 is attributable to the single documented downstream event rather than to systematic emulation coverage gaps.

Operational implications. For pipelines that (a) enforce parser‑validated inputs, (b) employ a validator whose rule-set aligns with expected intents, and (c) use single-shot generation semantics, adding always-on sandboxed emulation may produce negligible incremental detection benefit at scale. Conversely, guarded stages remain important where inputs are noisy or adversarial, where validator coverage is incomplete, or where emulation fidelity models production control-plane subtleties. In practice operators can trade between investing in richer static validators for throughput-sensitive paths and enabling selective guarded sandboxing for high‑risk changes.

Limitations and scope. The near-zero aggregate effect is specific to the preregistered task bank, single validator implementation, declared/requested model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed ~0.0014 effect lies well below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; archived per-episode artifacts permit auditors to locate and inspect that unique pair. We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design; extensions to adversarial, broader vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation remain necessary to identify regimes where guarded stages add substantive operational value. The archived execution bundle provides canonical artifacts and per-episode traces to support reproducible follow-up work.

limitations: Synthetic, parser-validated task bank and deterministic task generator reduce ecological diversity and produce a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit cross-model and cross-validator generalizability.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production control-plane behaviors and extended stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
